deities: Chintpurni Devi (worshipped in pindi form as Chhinnamastika, the severed-head goddess)

history.summary: Major Shakti Peeth shrine on a Sola Singhi Range ridge, where tradition says Sati's feet (some sources say forehead - conflicting, verify) fell, making the goddess Chintpurni, who 'removes all worries'. The present shrine is traditionally attributed to Pandit Mai Das (Bhai Mai Dass), a Saraswat Brahmin devotee, about 26 generations ago; one source instead credits a 19th-century construction by Maharaja Gulab Singh (conflicting, verify). Priestly duties remain with Mai Das's descendants. Four ancient Shiva temples (Kaleshwar, Narayana, Muchkund Mahadev, Shiva Bari) surround the peeth. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Una'; the temple is in Himachal Pradesh.

name: Chintpurni Temple
town_description: Chintpurni is a pilgrim town in Una district on a ridge along the Dharamshala-Hoshiarpur road, on one of the highest peaks of the Sola Singhi Range. It sits near Bharwain (pin 177110) and is one of the most visited Shakti shrines in North India, drawing lakhs of devotees at Navratri.

travel.airport: Kangra (Gaggal) Airport, then road via Bharwain
travel.railway: Una or Hoshiarpur (Punjab) railway stations, then road
travel.road: On the Dharamshala-Hoshiarpur road; well connected by bus and taxi

visitor_information.best_time: Navratri (March-April and September-October); the Shravan fair in July-August
visitor_information.opening_hours: Darshan timings vary seasonally; verify with the temple authorities before visiting
